item.title: Mackinaw City, NMCA advance to MHSAA district volleyball finals
item.description: MACKINAW CITY — Mackinaw City will play for an MHSAA Division 4 district volleyball title . Taking on Mackinac Island in a district semifinal , the Comets booked their ticket to a championship clash at St. Ignace by capturing a 3-0 victory (25-12, 25-11, 25-16) over the Lakers in Mackinaw City on Tuesday, Nov. 3. MACK CITY'S RIAN ESPER: Esper a key Mackinaw City volleyball player in many different spots MACK CITY BOYS QUALIFY FOR XC STATES: Area's top performers paced by state-qualifier Mackinaw City boys XC DISTRICT VOLLEYBALL PREVIEW: Previewing, predicting Cheboygan-area volleyball district tournaments After starting slow and trailing 7-1 in the first set, the Comets (13-22-5) regrouped, battled back and took a one-set lead in the match. From there, they were in cruise control behind quality offensive and defensive play. "Once we were able to get ourselves settled, we played some very solid volleyball tonight and did a great job of getting into our system offensively, and our defense did a great job of digging balls and keeping balls alive to give ourselves a shot at winning some long volleys," Mackinaw City coach Jake Huffman said. Rian Esper's 10 kills, six aces and six digs fueled the Comets, who received 16 assists, seven digs, two kills and seven digs from Julia Short, and 11 digs, six assists, four kills and three aces from Emily Kruczynski. Mackinaw City's many other contributors included Alaia Mendez (eight kills, five aces, four digs), Poppy Wallace (five kills, two digs, one block), Ella Kruczynski (six aces, five digs, one assist), and Sarah Lentell (two kills, one dig). "I was very happy with our response and proud of the effort that ladies put forth tonight," Huffman said. "We will use (Wednesday) to prep for a very tough St. Ignace squad on Thursday." Thursday's district final at St. Ignace (10-11-7) is a 6 p.m. start. item.title: Caitlin Clark’s latest heartwarming gesture sees her send a massive gift to her alma mater
item.description: Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark had her former college team, the Iowa Hawkeyes, in mind after the Nike CC1 release. Clark dominated the NCAA with a four-year stint with the Hawkeyes. Although she never won a national championship, losing in the 2023 and 2024 finals, she set countless records for the college and the NCAA as a whole. Now with her third WNBA season in the rearview, Clark showed love to where she became a national superstar by sending a gift over to the current women’s basketball team on the Hawkeyes. Caitlin Clark gifts CC1s to Iowa Hawkeyes women’s basketball team Clark sent over custom black-and-gold Nike Caitlin 1 signature shoes to the Hawkeyes, creating a player-exclusive Iowa PE colorway for their season-opener against Towson. The team shared a video of the excited reactions current players had to the gift. The Hawkeyes also shared an in-game picture of how the sneakers looked on the players’ feet during the game. While Clark has previously gifted sneakers to the Hawkeyes team, including pairs of the CC1s, this is the first time she has created a team-exclusive PE for the players, featuring the University of Iowa Tigerhawk logo on the tongue. The Hawkeyes picked up a convincing 73-45 win over the Towson Tigers in their CBB season-opener on November 3. Junior Dani Carnegie, who was a freshman during Clark’s final year with the Hawkeyes, led them to the win with 21 points, five rebounds and five assists. Clark left the Hawkeyes without a championship, but set the NCAA Division 1 basketball scoring record with 2,951 points, breaking Pete Maravich’s 54-year-old 3,667-point record. She has also made the most three-pointers in NCAA history with 548, with her 201 threes in 23-24 setting the record for most in one season. Her legacy as a Hawkeye is arguably richer than any current professional athlete due to the historic nature of her four-year tenure. While not having a championship to cement it as the greatest NCAA career of all time is rough, she gave Iowa years of incredible basketball. item.description: Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez during the Premier League match between Everton and Chelsea at Hill Dickinson Stadium in Liverpool, United Kingdom, on October 17, 2026. (Photo by Alfie Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images There’s an international break after this weekend’s matches, but for a fair few Chelsea boys, there will be no rest. And among those set for national team duty are our trio or Argentinians. Trio? — you might ask. Who all could that be? After all, Enzo Fernández is gone. Alejandro Garnacho is gone. And Emi Martínez has a broken face. Who’s left? Valentín Barco. Sure. Get in the chopper! But joining Barco are indeed Martínez, and, in an even bigger surprise, Aarón Anselmino — man with no actual minutes of competitive senior football yet this season. Maybe Argentina just want their own Estêvão situation. Argentina are playing only a couple friendlies during this break, against Uruguay and Costa Rica, and manager Lionel Scaloni is using this opportunity to check out some fresh faces. Anselmino is one of two players called up with zero senior caps, and one of nine with less than five. (Barco himself is barely above that threshold at seven.) And Emi’s inclusion is hopefully a good sign that is recovery from the fractured jaw he suffered against Everton a few weeks ago is going well. item.title: Lightning’s Nikita Kucherov has been on fire since trade request
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Lightning’s Nikita Kucherov has been on fire since trade request appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Nikita Kucherov wants out of the Tampa Bay Lightning , but he still can’t stop going all out for his team. Reports surfaced last Friday that the 33-year-old Kucherov had already asked the Lightning to move him. In the two games since, the two-time Hart Memorial Trophy winner has done nothing on the ice but rack up points. Against the Nashville Predators on Saturday on the road, Kucherov had a hand in three of his team’s goals, as he recorded a trio of assists, albeit in a 5-4 shootout loss to Steven Stamkos and company. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Bolts returned to action on Tuesday, and Kucherov was clearly still feeling it, adding two more assists to his total in the 2026-27 NHL season. This time around, his effort did not go for naught, with the Lightning defeating the Detroit Red Wings, 4-2. Kucherov is in a contract year, which means he is on track to become a free agent next summer. However, he also clarified that his trade request is less about money and more about the perceived disrespect he feels from Tampa Bay over its “poor communication.” It remains to be seen how this saga between Kucherov and the Lightning will conclude, but what seems to be clear is that he is not shortchanging the only team he’s played for so far in his NHL career when it comes to his effort and production on the ice. Kucherov and the Lightning improved to 9-3-2 after the win against Detroit. Up next for them is a date with the visiting Chicago Blackhawks on Thursday. item.title: Ex-Broncos QB Russell Wilson Interviewed for FBS Head Coaching Job
item.description: Denver Broncos head coach Russell Wilson. Getty Former Denver Broncos quarterback Russell Wilson could be headed for a major career shift less than one year after the end of his NFL career. “Former Super Bowl champion quarterback Russell Wilson interviewed Tuesday for the head coaching job at NC State, ” ESPN’s Adam Schefter wrote on Tuesday night. “Wilson, 38, joins Philip Rivers as former NC State and NFL quarterbacks who are now prominent candidates for the Wolfpack job. NC State fired Dave Doeren as head coach on Oct. 24. Wilson played at NC State from 2008 to 2010 before transferring to Wisconsin in 2011. After being taken by Seattle in the third round of the 2012 NFL draft, he went on to play 14 seasons in the NFL, leading the Seahawks to their first Super Bowl championship in the 2013 season.” Wilson, a 10-time NFL All-Pro, retired in June and has been working for CBS Sports as an analyst this fall. “Interesting that Russell Wilson and Philip Rivers are contenders,” NFL reporter Ed Werder wrote on his official X account on Tuesday. Wilson spent his first 10 seasons with the Seattle Seahawks , where he won one Super Bowl and played in another before a blockbuster trade to the Broncos before the 2022 season. He lasted 2 seasons in Denver before spending one season each with the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Giants . Broncos’ Wilson Trade One of NFL’s All-Time Worst Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox called the Broncos’ trade with the Seahawks for Wilson “Worst NFL Trade of the Last 10 Years” for the franchise. By releasing Wilson in April 2024, the Broncos were forced to take an NFL-record $85 million dead cap hit spread across the 2024 and 2025 seasons. “The Denver Broncos’ ill-fated 2022 trade for Russell Wilson has largely been overshadowed by the disastrous deal Cleveland made for Deshaun Watson in the same offseason,” Knox wrote. “However, that doesn’t mean that Denver’s deal was a good one. In fact, the Wilson trade might be considered the worst of the last decade if not for the Watson debacle. The Broncos coughed up two first-round picks, two second-round picks, a fifth-round pick, quarterback Drew Lock , defensive lineman Shelby Harris and tight end Noah Fant to acquire Wilson and a fourth-round pick. The Broncos then signed Wilson to an extension worth $242.6 million over five years with $161 million guaranteed.” Russell Wilson, Sean Payton Butted Heads in 2023 The writing was on the wall for Wilson once Nathaniel Hackett was fired after one season as Denver’s head coach in 2022 and replaced with former New Orleans Saints head coach and Super Bowl champion Sean Payton. Wilson and Payton famously butted heads, but the bottom line was that Wilson went 11-19 over 2 seasons in Denver before he was released. Wilson rejuvenated his career somewhat in 2024 with the Pittsburgh Steelers on a 1-year, $1.2 million contract. LOS ANGELES – The Los Angeles Lakers ’ current win streak hit two games following their 138-117 thrashing of the Miami Heat on Monday, and the team welcomed the return of forward Ziaire Williams. The six-year veteran had been sidelined for three games due to a foot injury , but he was cleared to go, picking up right where he left off prior to sitting out. Although Ziaire Williams had been in the starting lineup to begin the season, he came off the Lakers’ bench in the win against the Heat, contributing nine points on 3-of-6 shooting from the 3-point line. Williams has been one of the team’s most dependable 3&D players , along with Matisse Thybulle, and for him, the uptick in his shooting efficiency is due to the players he’s playing alongside. “They’re easy looks, way easier than they’ve been in the past. Like I said, they’re sending two to Luka [Doncic], two to AR [Austin Reaves] every time,” Williams said during his postgame press conference after the win against the Heat. “It’s just swing, swing, one more and I get to set my feet, get to square up the ball. I put a lot of work this summer. [I’m] trusting my work, confident in my shot, my shot feels great. I put the reps in, so I just got to trust it.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Through five games this season, Williams is shooting career-highs across the board. According to ESPN insider Adam Schefter, Wilson interviewed for the program’s head coaching vacancy Tuesday. His involvement adds another recognizable name to a search that already includes Philip Rivers. For Wolfpack fans, the connection is obvious. Both quarterbacks starred at NC State before building lengthy NFL careers. Now, the program is considering whether that experience and familiarity could translate into leadership from the sideline. Russell Wilson Interviews for NC State Opening Wilson played three seasons for NC State from 2008 through 2010 before transferring to Wisconsin. He later led Seattle to a Super Bowl championship and became one of the NFL’s most recognizable quarterbacks. After retiring in June, he joined CBS Sports as an analyst. The reported interview introduces a different possibility for his next football chapter. Broadcasting allows Wilson to explain the game from outside the building. Coaching would require him to shape everything happening inside it, from player development to the staff responsible for executing his vision. The Australian is currently on a two-fight losing streak after dropping the welterweight title to Islam Makhachev at UFC 322 in November 2025 . item.description: HOUSTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 16: Bryan Woo #22 of the Seattle Mariners pitches the ball during the first inning against the Houston Astros at Daikin Park on August 16, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) Getty The Seattle Mariners have settled the biggest question of the offseason by hiring their new manager Jason Kanzler, but now the question of how they will go about trying to improve the roster comes to the fore. Buster Olney dropped a really interesting tidbit on what the Mariners may try to do in the offseason as it related to the team’s pitching surplus. Here is an excerpt from what Olney wrote: “I’ve heard Seattle is poking around to assess how its surplus in pitching might be used to add a bat.” However, he also stipulates that intense trade talks are probably not going to occur until after a new CBA is negotiated so teams have a better sense of what their financial situations are going to be. Still, it makes total sense for the Mariners to explore trading away a pitcher or two to try and improve the offense. Seattle was one of the worst teams in MLB offensively in 2026 and ranked 28th in runs per game. While the offense was poor, the Mariners have a lot of solid starting pitchers. Whether it’s Logan Gilbert, Bryan Woo, George Kirby, or Emerson Hancock, there is really no shortage of options if they want to thin things out a bit especially since Kade Anderson debuted and looked solid. Mariners should talk to teams in need of starting pitching Seattle would be wise to engage in talks with teams that are in desperate need of starting pitching. The Chicago Cubs make a lot of sense since basically their entire starting staff is set to hit free agency and they are bound to lose at least a couple of arms. Matt Shaw could be an interesting position player for the Mariners to target. The San Francisco Giants are another team that could use some starters. Logan Webb, Landen Roupp, and Adrian Houser should all be in the starting rotation but they have two spots that need filling. Maybe the Mariners could try to get Casey Schmitt who hit 21 home runs in 98 games last season. Another team to keep an eye on is the San Diego Padres . Michael King, Casey Mize, Robbie Ray, and Nick Pivetta are all hitting free agency so they will likely need to replenish the rotation. Perhaps Jake Cronenworth or Xander Bogaerts could make sense as a boost to the lineup. Don’t expect any sort of deal this month like Olney said, but the Mariners are well-positioned to score a bat so they’d be foolish not to trade away a starter or two in order to improve on offense. item.description: Bethlehem junior June McCarthy and Ballston Spa senior Leah Szmarz race to the ball during the Section 2, Class AA finals on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, at Shaker High School in Colonie, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) LATHAM - First-year Bethlehem girls' soccer coach Scott Geis spent plenty of time getting his team ready for a potentially season-deciding slate of penalty kicks. Tuesday night at Shaker High School, that work paid off. The Eagles played to a thrilling 1-1 draw with Ballston Spa after 110 minutes in the Section 2 Class AA championship game, but Bethlehem stamped its ticket to the state tournament, advancing 4-2 on penalty kicks. "We practice it non-stop," Geis said. "We practice it with me in the goal. … I would shout, ‘Hey, this is the most important shot you've ever taken.' Just pressure, pressure, pressure - and, each time, they laughed it off, they breathed through it and they put it home just like they did today." No. 2 seed Bethlehem (10-4-4 overall) got a huge momentum burst to start the PKs when junior goalie Kinley Logsdon made a diving save to deny Ballston Spa's first shooter, Abby Werner. It was Logsdon's first-ever round of PKs in high school, but she's been through them at the club level. "I know the pressure," she said. "I know I can deal with it." The fifth-seeded Scotties (9-5-5 overall) were also denied in PKs when Charlotte Haskell's attempt hit the post. All four Bethlehem players who stepped up to the penalty spot - Maira Braddock, June McCarthy, Mallory Maycrink and Elayna Shersky - calmly converted their attempts. "As soon as I got it on frame, I knew we had it in the bag," Braddock said. "We've done this so many times in practice. It was just constant repetition. It felt the same.
